terms.gloss: satisfy, fill up (hunger, thirst, a desire)
evidence: Cic. Sen. 26 (Lewis & Short): quasi diūturnam sitim explēre cupiēns
terms.comment: Literally “fill full”; so to satisfy a need as if filling it with food: famem, sitim, cupiditātem, dēsīderium explēre (Lewis & Short). It also means to complete a number or a time, and to make good a loss.
To give enough or more than enough, so often “glut”, of hunger, anger or hatred. Not to be confused with satiō, satiōnis, a sowing.

phrases.latin: dēscende, amīce; tanta bonitās est aquae, voluptās ut satiārī nōn possit mea
phrases.english: come down, friend; the water is so good that I can’t get enough of it

phrases.latin: quās (litterās Graecās) sīc avidē arripuī quasi diūturnam sitim explēre cupiēns
phrases.english: which (Greek literature) I seized as greedily as if I wanted to quench a long thirst
